questions.text: Describe a time when you learned something from a mistake.
questions.say: Thank you. Now, in Part 2, I'm going to give you a topic, and I'd like you to talk about it for one to two minutes. Before you talk, you'll have one minute to think about what you're going to say. You can make some notes if you wish. Here is your topic. Describe a time when you learned something from a mistake. You should say: what the mistake was; when it happened; what the result of the mistake was; and explain what you learned from it.

questions.text: Do you think you would make the same mistake again?
questions.say: Thank you. Do you think you would make the same mistake again?

questions.text: Why are some people afraid of making mistakes?
questions.say: Thank you. We've been talking about a time when you learned from a mistake, and I'd like to discuss with you some more general questions related to this. Let's consider first of all learning from mistakes. Why are some people afraid of making mistakes?

questions.text: Should teachers correct every mistake that students make?
questions.say: Should teachers correct every mistake that students make?

questions.text: Can children learn more from their own mistakes than from advice?
questions.say: Can children learn more from their own mistakes than from advice?

questions.text: How should a manager tell an employee that they have done something wrong?
questions.say: Now let's talk about criticism and feedback. How should a manager tell an employee that they have done something wrong?

questions.text: Why do some people find it hard to accept criticism?
questions.say: Why do some people find it hard to accept criticism?

questions.text: Is online feedback, such as product reviews, useful?
questions.say: Is online feedback, such as product reviews, useful?
